 :JUDGMENT:
This is a Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- for the death of Mandala Karthik, in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 17.07.2022 at about 5.45 a.m., Mandal Karthik was proceeding as a rider on his Motor Cycle slowly, cautiously by observing traffic rules and regulations from north to south direction on 8th Main Road, J.P. Nagar 3rd Phase in order to reach his house.

When he entered the junction, the rider of Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JF-8144 drove the vehicle in a rash or negligent manner, with high speed, came to extreme right side and dashed against the motor cycle in which the Mandal Karthik was proceeding.
As a result, the Mandal Karthik thrown on the road and sustained fatal injuries all over the body.
Immediately he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, in-spite of better treatment, he was succumbed to injuries at about 6.15 a.m.

Body of the deceased Mandal Karthik was shifted to KIMS Hospital,
wherein postmortem was conducted.
The petitioners have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies of deceased.
It is stated that, 1st petitioner is the wife, 2 nd and 3rd petitioners are the parents of the deceased.

At the time of accident, deceased was aged 25 years and he was completed Diploma in Therapist and working as Restoratory Therapist at SDC TRC and Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Chest Diseases (Government of Karnataka) and getting salary of Rs.21,400/- per month.

entities.text: Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Chest Diseases (Government of Karnataka)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The deceased was working in night hours and he was free in morning, hence, he was also working in private hospital and getting additional income.
In total he was earning Rs.31,400/- per month and contributing his entire earnings towards welfare of the family.

The 1st petitioner lost her loving Nagalakshmi vs Santhosh.H on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198705949/
2 husband and 2nd and 3rd petitioners lost their only son and they are living in a miserable condition.

The accident was occurred only due to rash or negligent riding of the rider of Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JF- 8144 and Jayanagar Traffic police have registered the case against the rider of offending vehicle.
The 1st respondent is the insured and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the aforesaid vehicle, hence, the petitioners claim compensation from the respondents.
With these averments petitioners prayed to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st and 2nd respondents have appeared through their counsel and filed written statements.

4. The written statement averments of 1st respondent is as hereunder:
Respondent No.1- R.C.
Owner of the offending vehicle has denied the entire averments of the petition.

The 1 st respondent has contended that, the accident was not occurred due to rash or negligent riding of the offending vehicle by the 1 st respondent, but it was due to rash or negligence of the deceased.

Though this respondent also sustained grievous injuries and he was survived after prolonged treatment in the hospital, he has lodged the complaint against the deceased, but the police have not registered the criminal case against the deceased as he was died in the accident.
As such the petition is not maintainable and bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

The 1 st respondent has contended that, the offending vehicle was insured with the 2 nd respondent as on the date of accident and the 1 st respondent who is the rider of offending vehicle was also holding valid D.L.

On the other hand,
the deceased was riding the vehicle as he was sleepy and he had no valid D.L. at the time of accident.

The deceased was also not wearing helmet at the time of accident,
which is visible in CC TV footage.
It is contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant.
In case of awarding compensation, the 2nd respondent is liable to pay the same.
With these averments, the 1st respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. The written statement averments of 2 nd respondent is as hereunder:
Respondent No.2-Insurance Company has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending vehicle, however contended that, liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

The accident occurred due to self negligence of the deceased or some other vehicle and the petitioners have suppressed the said fact and filed the false case against this respondent to claim compensation by colluding with the police and insured.
The R.C. owner of the offending vehicle has not complied the mandatory duty as per Sec.134(c) of M.V. Act.
Further the police have not complied the mandatory duty as per Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.

The 1 st respondent has violated the policy conditions by entrusting his Honda Active bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JF-8144 Nagalakshmi vs Santhosh.H on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198705949/
3 to the rider, who had no valid D.L. to drive the said vehicle.

The 2 nd respondent denied the rash or negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, death of deceased due to injuries sustained in the accident, age, occupation and income of deceased, amount spent by the petitioners.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive.
With these averments, the 2nd respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:
: I S S U E S:
1. Whether petitioners prove that Mandala Karthik was died on 17.07.2022 due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of rider of Honda Activa bearing Registration No.KA-05-JF-8144 as stated in the petition?
2.
Whether R2 proves the alleged rash and negligent driving of the Deceased as contended in para 9 of the written statement?
3. Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
5. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.
Two witnesses were examined as P.W.2 and P.W.3 and Ex.P.18 to Ex.P.21 were marked through P.W.3.
Thereafter, P.W.1 to 3 subject to the process of cross-examination.
Respondents have not adduced any evidence.
8. Heard the arguments of both side.
Perused the materials placed on record.

The findings of the Tribunal to the above referred issues are as under:
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- In the Negative.
Issue No.3 :- In the Partly Affirmative.

Issue No.4 :- In the Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.5 :- As per the final order for the following:

ISSUE Nos.1 and 2:-
These issues are inter connected.
Hence, they have taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition.
10. It is the case of the petitioners that, on 17.07.2022 at about 5.45 a.m., deceased Mandala Karthik was returning to house from his duty in his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05- LB-8005.

While he was proceeding on 8 th Main road, J.P. Nagar, a Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JF-8144 being driven by its rider in a rash or negligent manner with high speed and dashed to vehicle in which the deceased was proceeding.
Due to impact, deceased fell down and sustained fatal injuries and he succumbed to injuries.
11. In order to prove the case, the 1 st petitioner examined herself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of her oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
In order to prove the issue No.1, P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.17.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of Complaint.
Ex.P.2 is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.92/2022.
Ex.P.3 is the true copy spot mahazar.
Ex. P.4
is the true copy of spot sketch.
Ex.P.5 is the true copy of Postmortem report.
Ex.P.6 is the true copy of M.V.A. report.
Ex.P.7 is the true copy of charge and Ex.P.17 is the true copy of inquest report.
12. Petitioners have also examined one eye witness namely Sadhu Raghavendra Rao as P.W.2.

P.W.2 has deposed that, on 17.07.2022 at about 5.45 a.m., when he was going to meet his friend at Jayanagara and he reached near 3 rd Cross, 8th Main, J.P. Nagar junction, he saw the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LB-8005 slowly and cautiously by observing traffic rules.

When the rider of said vehicle almost crossed the 8th Main, 3rd Cross junction, at that time the rider of Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JF-8144 came in a rash or negligent manner with high speed and dashed to right side of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LB-8005.
Due to impact, the rider of said vehicle feel down and sustained fatal injuries.

Further deposed that, later he came to know that,
his name is Karthik and he was died in the casualty in NIMHANS hospital on the same day.
P.W.2 was cross-examined by the counsel for the 1st respondent and 2nd respondent.
13. Now the important question before this Tribunal is to find whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent riding of offending vehicle or not?
In order to answer this aspect, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7.
On careful perusal of these documents, it is crystal clear that, criminal case was registered against the rider of the offending vehicle.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the rider of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.7.
It is relevant to note that, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 have contended that, the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased himself, he was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
However, in order to substantiate the same, the respondents have not placed any material before this Tribunal.
Apart from that, the 1 st respondent himself is the rider of offending was also not examined to substantiate his own contentions.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.

The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been Nagalakshmi vs Santhosh.H on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198705949/
5 applied".
14. The above referred decision is aptly applicable to the case on hand.
At the cost of repetition, the Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle bearing No.05-JF-8144.

Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent riding of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.05-JF-8144 by its rider.
The 2nd respondent failed to prove that, the accident was occurred due to negligent riding of deceased.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative and Issue No.2 is answered in the Negative.
15. ISSUE No.3:-
This issue is is with regard to age and income of the deceased.
Age:- In the instant case, the respondent No.2 has disputed the age of the deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 25 years.
In order to substantiate the same, P.W.1 has not produced any material documents.
The petitioners have produced the notarized copy of driving licence pertaining to deceased Mandala Karthi available on record, the date of birth was mentioned as 13.07.1997.
Apart from that, the 1st petitioner is aged about 24 years.
The 1st petitioner is the wife of deceased.
The accident was occurred on 17.07.2022.
By considering the age of 1st petitioner, it can be inferred that, the deceased was aged about 25 years at the time of accident.
16. Income:- Now, the next aspect is with respect to income of deceased.

According to the petitioners, the deceased was started his work at Apollo Hospital, Jayanagar, Bangalore and as he got good opportunity, he joined SDS TRC and Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Chest Diseases, Bangalore in the month of January-2022 for a monthly salary of Rs.21,400/-.

entities.text: Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Chest Diseases, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: P.W.1 has stated that, the deceased apart from working in the above hospital, he was also working at private hospital on part time basis and he was totally getting Rs.31,400/- per month.
However, to substantiate the income of the deceased, P.W1 has produced Ex.P.13 i.e., bank pass book of the deceased Mandala Karthik.
17. In order to substantiate the income of deceased, the petitioners have examined one witness namely Ragini V., Chief Accounts Officer, Rajeev Gandhi Hospital, Bengalur as P.W.3.
P.W.3 has deposed that, deceased was appointed as Sleep Lab Technician and his salary was fixed at Rs.21,400/-.
In order to substantiate her evidence, she has produced Ex.P.18 to Ex.P.21.

As per Ex.P.19, the deceased was appointed under Stipendiary basis and his salary was fixed at Rs.21,400/-
and he was appointed on 02.07.2022.
However, the petitioners have not produced any document to substantiate that, the deceased was earning Rs.31,400/- per month.
Hence, the income of deceased is considered as Rs.21,400/- per month.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.4:- This issue is with regard to entitlement of relief.
According to the petition averments, petitioner No.1 is the wife of deceased, petitioner No.2 is the father and petitioner No.3 is the mother of deceased.
The 1st petitioner has lost her husband.
2nd and 3rd petitioners being the parents of deceased have lost their son.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.
Hence, petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of deceased.

Keeping in view of the 3 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/3rd of the amount is to be deducted from total Nagalakshmi vs Santhosh.H on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198705949/
6 income toward the personal expenses of deceased.

19. Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioners have established the age of deceased i.e.,
as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 25 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident,
the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
"If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".
"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
20.
Admittedly, the petitioners have produced documents to show the income of deceased.
The deceased was aged about 25 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
In the instant case, the deceased was 25 years.

Hence, the future prospects of 40%
is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling 40% of the Rs.21,400/- has to be added to monthly income of deceased, which comes to Rs.8,560/-.

So,
monthly income of deceased is taken at Rs.21,400/- + Rs.8,560/- = Rs.29,960/-.
In this case petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the 3 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/3rd amount is to be deducted toward personal expenses.
From this his personal living expenses which should be 1/3rd of Rs.29,960/- has to be deducted.

Thereby,
the actual income will come to Rs.29,960/- - Rs.9,986/- =Rs.19,974/-.

Then total income of the deceased per annum comes to Rs.2,39,688/- (Rs.19,974 x 12 =2,39,688/-)
21.
As the deceased was 25 years old at the time of death, the multiplier 18 is applied, which is appropriate to age of deceased.
The normal compensation would then workout to be Rs.2,39,688/- x 18 = Rs.43,14,384/- for loss of dependency.

22. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: P.W.1 has stated that, they have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards performing final rites of deceased.
In this regard, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Now, the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioners Nos.2 and 3 are also entitled for consortium or not?
Admittedly, the 1 st petitioner is the wife and she is entitled for spousal consortium.
Admittedly, the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the parents of deceased.
At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.

It is relevant to note that, the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs.
Nagalakshmi vs Santhosh.H on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198705949/
7

entities.text:
National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs.
Nagalakshmi vs Santhosh.H on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pranay Sethi and Others Case, observed that, the conventional heads namely filial consortium, loss of estate, funeral expenses has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
Therefore, the 1st petitioner is entitled for Rs.44,000/- under the head of spousal consortium and petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.16,500/- is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards loss of estate.

23. The details of compensation amount is as under:
 S.No. Heads Rs.
 1. Towards loss of Rs. 43,14,384/-
 Dependency.
 2. Towards spousal and Rs. 1,32,000/-
 44,000 X 3  filial consortium,
 3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
 4.
Funeral expense Rs. 16,500/-

Hence, petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs. 44,79,384/-.
24.
Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:-
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that rider of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Hence, it is held that, the rider of offending vehicle was holding valid and effective D.L. as on the date of alleged accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:- Respondent No.2- the insurance company has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending vehicle.
Hence, it is held that, insurance coverage of the vehicle was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioners.

Interest:- In view of the decision reported in MFA NO:
30131-2019 dtd, 12.5.2020, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

Accordingly, this Tribunal is answered Issue No.5 in Partly Affirmative.
25. ISSUE No.6:-.
In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:

8
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.

Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.44,79,384/- (Rupees Forty Four Lakhs, Seventy Nine Thousand Three Hundred and Eighty Four Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.
 Respondent No.2 being insurer of the  offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 50%, petitioner No.2 is entitled for 25% and petitioner No.3 is entitled for 25% with interest.

Out of the adjudged compensation amount, 50% of share of petitioner Nos.1 to 3 with interest is to be paid to them by way of E- payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of their respective shares with interest shall be invested in F.D.
in their names in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years.

It is clarified that, the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.

3 to the rider, who had no valid D.L. to drive the said vehicle.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:

2.
Whether R2 proves the alleged rash and negligent driving of the Deceased as contended in para 9 of the written statement?
3. Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On careful perusal of these documents, it is crystal clear that, criminal case was registered against the rider of the offending vehicle.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the rider of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.7.
It is relevant to note that, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 have contended that, the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased himself, he was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
At the cost of repetition, the Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle bearing No.05-JF-8144.
Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent riding of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.05-JF-8144 by its rider.
The 2nd respondent failed to prove that, the accident was occurred due to negligent riding of deceased.
Age:- In the instant case, the respondent No.2 has disputed the age of the deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 25 years.
In order to substantiate the same, P.W.1 has not produced any material documents.
The petitioners have produced the notarized copy of driving licence pertaining to deceased Mandala Karthi available on record, the date of birth was mentioned as 13.07.1997.
Apart from that, the 1st petitioner is aged about 24 years.
The 1st petitioner is the wife of deceased.
The accident was occurred on 17.07.2022.
2nd and 3rd petitioners being the parents of deceased have lost their son.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.
Hence, petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of deceased.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident,
the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".
The deceased was aged about 25 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
In the instant case, the deceased was 25 years.
Hence, the future prospects of 40%
is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling 40% of the Rs.21,400/- has to be added to monthly income of deceased, which comes to Rs.8,560/-.
